The private space is a separate profile with its own copy of the app. While the space is locked, that copy is stopped and hidden from Deluge, Settings, search, recents and other launchers. The copy outside keeps its data until you remove it.
%1$s lives in your private space. Unlock the space to finish protecting it.
Install this app inside the private space, then come back. Deluge checks again and moves to the last step.
Deluge will install a fresh copy inside the private space. The copy outside keeps its data until you remove it.
Couldn\'t install %1$s in the private space
The copy outside can still be opened from Android Settings while the space is locked. Remove it to close that way in. App data does not move — set the app up again inside the private space.

Deluge is installed but Android is not using it yet. Set it as your default home app to see your favorites and the app list.

Disguises app names and icons for screenshots, and hides the status bar.
Switch to the dark theme in the evening and back in the morning, instead of following the system.
Skip the launcher\'s own transitions; opening the app list and its fades happen at once.
Two fingers on the home screen change the icon size.
Apps you have paused show dimmed, so they read as set aside. Turn off to list them like any other.
Needs the same notification access Now Playing does. Counts only unless notification text is turned on below
Shows the newest notification under the app name. Needs the same notification access. Off by default.

Rest your finger on a letter and the list walks on through its apps, for letters with a lot of them

Ready — pull down on the home screen
Pull down on the home screen. If nothing happens, enable Deluge Launcher under Accessibility — and if that switch is greyed out, allow restricted settings from App info first.
Used for Now Playing, notification counts, the panel and notification text
Choose which apps sit on the home screen
Stay in the list after unlocking
Unlocking Private Space keeps the app list open instead of going back to the home screen
Groups the private space apps below the alphabet instead of mixing them in, so the two copies of an app can be told apart
Ends the app list with whatever arrived most recently
Tap only the icon and name
A favorite opens only when you tap its icon or name, not anywhere along its line
Helps app names stand out over a busy wallpaper. Applied only behind light text, where it adds contrast rather than muddying it
Hide %1$s from the app list? You can put it back under Settings › Apps › Hidden apps.
Turning this off unfreezes everything and clears the list. Its rows and actions disappear.
%1$d apps will join the freeze list under %2$s. Nothing is frozen yet — run Freeze all when you are ready. System apps are included: freezing the wrong one can stop the device from booting.
%1$d apps will join the list under %3$s, and %2$d will leave it. Apps that leave and are frozen now will be unfrozen. Apps on another method\'s list are left alone.
%1$d apps could not be unfrozen while inverting, so they stay on the list.
Every frozen app is unfrozen first and the whole list is cleared. This cannot be undone; you will have to build the list again if you turn the feature back on.
App freezing is off. %1$d apps unfrozen and the list cleared.
%1$d apps could not be unfrozen, so app freezing stays on.
Freeze the list when the screen is off
Keeps a background service running, with a notification, while this is on.
Unfreeze when the screen is unlocked
States that the freeze list is being applied in the background.
The list is frozen a while after the screen goes off.
Freeze every app in the list
Pause every app in the list
Freezing needs root or Shizuku. Install Shizuku and grant it access, or run Deluge as root.
Recommended: Shizuku — no root needed, and freezing is faster than through su.
Hiding apps needs root. Disable and Suspend work without it.
Android 15\'s Private space is a separate profile with its own copy of each app. While it is locked, those apps are stopped and invisible to Deluge, other apps, search, recents and notifications.
Deluge shows the space as a padlock row at the end of the app list while it is your default launcher; tap it to unlock. Apps have to be installed again inside.
Unlike hiding, this is a real boundary: other apps cannot enumerate it. One space per device, main user only; it can share the phone with a work profile.
This system has no Private space settings page.
Freezing or hiding system apps can stop the device from booting. Only do it if you know how to recover.
Gone from the launcher and Settings, and no component of it can run in the background.
Stays disabled after a reboot, and some apps must be re-enabled here before they can update.
Looks uninstalled: gone from the launcher and Settings, data kept, cannot be started.
Needs root, and it is not a security boundary: apps that enumerate every package still see it.
Keeps the icon, greys it, hides notifications and blocks opening it, and stops background runs, without losing data.
Stops scheduled background work, but an app with special privileges can still get through.
%1$s is paused by Deluge. Tap the button to unpause it and open it.
Kills the running process at once and leaves nothing to undo.
Nothing is persisted: a broadcast or alarm can wake it again, so this is not a lasting freeze.
Off by default. System apps are left out of the freeze list.
Freezing or hiding a system app can stop the device from booting, break Settings or lose data. Continue only if you know how to recover with another device or recovery mode.
System apps will leave the freeze list, and any that are frozen right now will be unfrozen first.
System apps are hidden from the freeze list. Turn on "Show and freeze system apps" there first.
%1$d system apps could not be unfrozen, so system apps stay shown.
Do not freeze the app on screen
Read through root or Shizuku, so no usage-access permission is needed.
Do not freeze apps with notifications
Read through root or Shizuku, so no notification-listener permission is needed.
Frozen %1$d apps after the screen went off.
Automatic freeze skipped: no root or Shizuku access.
Automatic freeze skipped: the phone is charging.
Look for a newer release on GitHub
Allow Deluge to look at GitHub every time it starts and tell you when a new release is out. It only reads the version number, sends nothing about you, and never installs anything by itself.
Asked once on the first launch. While it is on, Deluge looks at its release page on startup (at most once an hour) and tells you when a new version is out.
Open the release page to download it
Version %1$s has been released. Open the release page to download it.

d day, M month, y year, E weekday. Repeat a letter for a longer form: d, dd, EEE, EEEE.
Reading your calendar needs permission. Nothing leaves the phone: Deluge has no network access.
Weather comes from a weather app that already has it, so Deluge needs no network access and never asks where you are. In Breezy Weather, turn on Settings → Widgets & Live Wallpaper → Data sharing.
